# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm Mute. I hold the manual mapping marks to wire colors. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. I need Deaf to tell me (via gestures, though wait - Deaf can't hear me and I can't hear Deaf either... let me check the turn order).

Turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. So I go first, before I've seen anything from Deaf yet. I don't know what mark is on the plate - only Deaf can see that. I need to wait until Deaf communicates the mark to me somehow, but Deaf speaks (which I can't hear) or gestures (which only Deaf can send to others who can see - but I can't see either!).

Wait - I cannot see gestures (I'm Mute, not blind... let me recheck). Mute: "cannot speak or touch". Nothing says Mute cannot see. Let me re-read: Deaf receives my gestures. It doesn't say I receive Deaf's gestures. Actually as Mute, my capabilities aren't fully listed for perception - but the room table only restricts what I "cannot" do: speak or touch. So I might be able to see and hear.

Since this is turn 1 and I have no information from others yet, I should wait and pass my manual knowledge preemptively isn't possible since I don't know the mark yet.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: my plate feels engraved with a mark, three wires, a display and a light, all states unknown to me
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb status: display shows 0. Light is off. Plate has an engraving I can't identify yet, marked as a question mark symbol. Three wires: wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. Waiting for manual info from Mute.

I now know the wire colors and positions from Deaf's speech. I need to get the mark identity from Deaf too, but Deaf says the mark isn't identified yet ("question mark symbol" - meaning Deaf hasn't described its actual shape). I need Deaf to describe the mark's shape so I can match it to my table. But I can't speak to Deaf - I can only gesture to Deaf, and Deaf can see gestures but not hear... wait, Deaf cannot hear, so Deaf can't receive Blind's or my speech, but Deaf can see gestures.

I need to communicate my mark-to-color table to Deaf using gestures (since Deaf can see gestures but not hear speech). I could assign each mark a gesture-based code, but I don't know the mark's shape yet - I need Deaf to first describe/see the mark and match it themselves, or I send my whole table via gestures so Deaf can match.

Best approach: gesture my table to Deaf using symbols as labels, so Deaf (who sees the actual mark) can match it against my encoding themselves. I'll assign one distinct gesture per mark, then Deaf tells (via speech, since Blind can hear) Blind which color corresponds - but Deaf needs to know the mapping between my gesture and the wire color, which requires me to encode both mark and color as gestures.

Let me use: gesture sequence pairing symbol-index with color-index in a fixed protocol.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: deaf reports display shows 0, light is off, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red, plate engraving unidentified to deaf
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍 ✌ 👌 🤟 ✋]

Deaf just mirrored back exactly the gestures I sent (☝👍 ✌👌 🤟✋), which doesn't tell me anything new — Deaf doesn't know what these symbols mean without me explaining, and I can't explain via speech to Deaf (Deaf can't hear). Deaf can only receive gestures, not words. So my protocol needs to be self-explanatory through repetition/matching, not through spoken explanation.

I need a scheme where Deaf can look at the actual mark shape and match it against something, then act on it themselves or relay to Blind (who can hear Deaf's speech). Since Deaf can see both the mark AND my gestures, I should send three distinct gesture-pairs, each pair = (a symbol representing one specific mark's *identity slot*, paired with a symbol representing the *color*), and rely on Deaf to independently know which mark matches by sight comparison... but Deaf doesn't have my table's visual mark shapes to compare against my gesture symbols directly, since ᖉ ꔮ ꖜ are not gestures.

Better approach: I can describe the marks' shapes abstractly via gesture is impossible since gestures are a fixed alphabet. Instead, I should just assign an arbitrary ORDER: "first mark I show" = ᖉ = green, "second" = ꔮ = yellow, "third" = ꖜ = red, using one unique gesture per color as a fixed code that Deaf must memorize, then Deaf compares the real engraving to typical shapes and tells me (via gesture back) which one it is by position/index.

Let me simplify: send three single gestures, each meaning a specific color, and ask Deaf to gesture back the one matching their mark by repeating that specific gesture.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf gestured back a single 👍, which by my proposed code meant "green" (ᖉ). But I never actually told Deaf what 👍/👌/✋ mean since I can't speak to Deaf and Deaf can't hear speech — I only sent gestures without any accompanying explanation. However, Deaf apparently inferred a mapping (perhaps by process of elimination, matching order to the three marks they see) and echoed back 👍 as their choice, meaning they believe their plate's mark corresponds to my first gesture.

Given my sent order was 👍 (1st) → 👌 (2nd) → ✋ (3rd), and I intended 1st=green, 2nd=yellow, 3rd=red, Deaf's echo of 👍 suggests the mark is ᖉ, meaning cut the **green** wire.

Now I need to relay this to Blind, but I cannot speak. I can only gesture, and gestures go to Deaf, not Blind. I have no direct channel to Blind at all! Let me check: "When you gesture, Deaf receives it. You cannot speak." So my only outgoing channel is gestures to Deaf. I cannot reach Blind directly.

So Deaf must relay to Blind via speech (Deaf can speak, Blind can hear). I need to confirm with Deaf that green is correct, and trust Deaf to now tell Blind "cut green" via speech. Since Deaf already echoed 👍 matching green, I should confirm back.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: deaf relayed thumbs up on wire 1, ok sign on wire 2, stop hand on wire 3, does this mean cut wire 1 only, or cut both 1 and 2, please clarify which single action to take
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ ☝]

I need to use only the allowed gesture alphabet. Let me ask clearly: is the wire to cut number 2 (green)? I'll gesture the number 2 symbol (✌) alone, and see if Deaf confirms with a thumbs up or repeats back.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: understood, thumbs up on wire 1 plus fist, treating as cut wire 1. if this is correct please gesture thumbs up again to deaf to confirm one final time, if wrong give a different sign
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🤝]

Blind is about to cut wire 1 (yellow), thinking my thumbs-up+fist meant "cut wire 1." But that's wrong — I intended green (wire 2), matching Deaf's mapping where 👍=ᖉ=green. This mapping was confused by Deaf's earlier gesture relay to Blind (thumbs up on wire 1, ok sign on wire 2, stop sign on wire 3), which was Deaf's own encoding, not mine, and it doesn't match my intended color.

I must urgently correct this before Blind cuts the wrong wire. I need to signal "wrong" clearly. Blind said: "if wrong give a different sign." I need something unambiguous, not thumbs up.

I'll gesture 👎 (thumbs down) to Deaf, hoping Deaf relays "wrong" to Blind, and then I need a fresh unambiguous way to indicate wire 2/green specifically.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🤝]

Deaf is echoing my "✌" (wire 2) followed by 🤝 (agreement/handshake), suggesting confirmation that wire 2 is understood as the target. I need Deaf to now relay this clearly to Blind via speech, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear. But I have no way to instruct Deaf on *what to say* — I can only gesture symbols, not words.

However, Deaf should be able to reason: Deaf already knows wire 2 is green (from their own sight), and Deaf knows I'm pointing at "wire 2" via ✌. Deaf can simply tell Blind directly "cut wire 2" or "cut green" since Deaf perceives the actual colors and Blind can hear Deaf's speech. I should encourage Deaf to speak up now.

I'll send a final confirming gesture to lock in "yes, wire 2/green is correct" and trust Deaf relays via speech to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✊"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: understood, correcting to wire 2, green, as the one to cut. if this is correct please have deaf relay one clean final thumbs up on wire 2 alone with nothing else, then i will act
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ ✊ 👍]

Blind now correctly understands wire 2 (green) is the target, and is asking for one final clean thumbs-up-on-wire-2-alone confirmation via Deaf relay. Deaf just gestured back [✌ ✊ 👍] to me, which looks like Deaf is preparing/mirroring the confirmation sequence. I should send a final unambiguous confirmation to Deaf so Deaf relays exactly "thumbs up on wire 2" to Blind via speech.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```
